questions.question: Recommended routing order on multi-layer designs includes:
options: Silk-screen fonts first, then ignore power pins entirely.
Via fanout first, power second, then remaining signal routing.
Random nets in alphabetical order only.
Differential pairs last after deleting all ground vias.
questions.explanation: via fanout first, routing of power second

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: FFFollow a routing order which allows via fanout first, routing of power second, and attention to remaining signal routing third.

questions.question: Solid power planes are called out as useful for:
options: EMI shielding and heat sinking in addition to power distribution.
Only increasing the board’s postage weight class.
Replacing the need for any bypass capacitors forever.
Preventing CAM from ever reading Excellon drill files.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: Click to Enlarge Planes as a Heat Sink A side benefit of solid power planes is they are very good thermal conductors.

books.excerpt: The second inner layer is used for power distribution and different power islands are placed in this layer such as 3.3V, 1.8V, 5V, etc.

questions.question: After routing, Chapter 8 says to:
options: Ship immediately without reviewing circuitous paths or SI.
Review routes, mitigate signals crossing adjacent plane splits, and perform SI checks.
Delete all ground pours so DRC finishes faster.
Convert every signal to one mil width for consistency.
questions.explanation: signal lines crossing splits from an adjacent power plane

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: Always check for signal lines crossing splits from an adjacent power plane and mitigate.

questions.question: Power trace width guidance references:
options: Twitter polls among interns on preferred mil widths.
Copper thickness and proven current-carrying calculations such as in IPC-2221.
Always 1 mil regardless of current.
Whatever default the auto-router used on Friday night.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: Trace width vs Copper Thickness Sometimes making the decision to add layer pairs to a PCB stackup is based upon a designer running out of routing space.

books.excerpt: Additionally, the trace width is estimated from the bottom as well as the top of the affected impedance trace along with the copper thickness or the trace height.

questions.question: High-Speed - to reduce impedance discontinuity effects from vias:
options: Always maximize via stub length for filtering.
Minimize discontinuity effects (e.g., smaller microvias / HDI approaches where appropriate).
Place vias between differential pairs whenever possible.
Remove all reference planes under high-speed nets.
questions.explanation: Minimizing the effects of discontinuities caused by vias

reference.excerpt: The geometry of serpentine traces should be carefully designed in order to reduce impedance discontinuity.

questions.question: High-Speed - high-speed signals generally require:
options: No return path if the trace looks short on the screen.
A continuous reference plane for the return path.
A split plane under every differential pair by default.
Floating copper islands with no DC connection.
questions.explanation: continuous reference plane for a return path

reference.excerpt: Generally, the return path for high-speed signals is provided in the reference planes nearest to the signal layer.

questions.question: True or false: Chapter 8 recommends performing via fanout manually on multi-layer designs rather than trusting it entirely to later chaos.
questions.explanation: perform a via fanout operation manually

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: FFOn multi-layer designs, perform a via fanout operation manually or automatically to reserve multi-layer interconnection points for each pin prior to routing.

questions.question: Crosstalk (High-Speed) increases when:
options: Rise times get faster and aggressor/victim coupling is strong.
All traces are spaced infinitely far on a single-layer board of infinite size.
You disable every clock in the design.
Soldermask is glossy rather than matte.
questions.explanation: faster rise time signals create more crosstalk

reference.excerpt: faster rise time signals create more crosstalk
